claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is a single-phase FCC material.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is coarse-grained and lacks engineered nanoscale structural heterogeneity.
Trace Ti, Nb, or similar additions to CoCrFeNi can be processed to form stable nanoprecipitates.
Introducing nanoprecipitates will establish a nanohierarchical heterostructure in CoCrFeNi.
The engineered architecture will contain nano-coupled grains and uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates.
At lower temperatures, the nanohierarchical structure will enable multiple plastic-deformation pathways.
The multiple deformation pathways will partition or release localized frictional stress.
Lower localized stress and strain will reduce friction at lower temperatures.
At elevated temperatures, the nanoprecipitates will act as nucleation sites for rapid in situ tribo-oxidation.
Elevated-temperature sliding will produce a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer on the engineered material.
The nanocrystalline glaze layer will mitigate adhesive wear.
The nanocrystalline glaze layer will mitigate oxidative wear.
The nanoprecipitate-engineered CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower and more stable coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
The nanoprecipitate-engineered CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
At the high-temperature end, the engineered CoCrFeNi wear rate will approach 10^-7 to 10^-6 mm^3/N·m.
Conventionally processed CoCrFeNi typically exhibits increasing friction as temperature rises, particularly at high temperature.
Conventionally processed CoCrFeNi typically exhibits increasing wear as temperature rises, particularly at high temperature.
The proposed improvement is expected in ambient-air sliding from room temperature to 800 °C under a load of about 5 N.
Adequate oxygen availability may be required for formation of the high-temperature tribo-oxide glaze.
